name: SEN54 environmental sensor node
description: Sensirion all-in-one air quality module: particulate matter PM1.0/PM2.5/PM4.0/PM10 (0–1000 µg/m³, laser scattering with a built-in fan), relative humidity, temperature and VOC Index (1–500), a new reading every second (no NOx sensor: that output always reads unknown). The sensor needs 5 V; the adapter's AP3602A charge pump makes 5 V from a 3–5 V supply and the adapter has 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups and ties SEL to GND. I2C address 0x69, 100 kHz. Sold as: Sensirion SEN54-SDN-T plugged into the Adafruit SEN54 or SEN55 Adapter Breakout - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 5964) with a 6-pin JST GH cable; 4-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA.
eli5: A small box with a fan that sniffs the air and tells you how much dust and smelly gases are in it, plus the temperature and humidity.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Adapter supply, 3–5 V (use the microcontroller's logic voltage); a charge pump makes the sensor's 5 V. Draws about 150 mA from 3.3 V while measuring

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, 10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the adapter, 3–5 V logic

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, 10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the adapter, 3–5 V logic

supplierQuery: Sensirion SEN54-SDN-T environmental sensor node + Adafruit 5964 SEN5x adapter
buildNotes: Plug the SEN54 into the adapter's JST GH socket with a 6-pin GH cable (1.25 mm pitch); the adapter wires sensor pin 5 (SEL) to GND so the sensor starts in I2C mode.

Power VIN from the board's 3.3 V (or 5 V on a 5 V board): the adapter's AP3602A charge pump makes the sensor's 5 V (4.5–5.5 V). From 3.3 V expect about 150 mA while the fan runs (roughly twice the sensor's 70 mA), more in the first 60 s.
The adapter has 10 kΩ pull-ups on SDA and SCL to VIN, so no extra resistors are needed. Keep the bus at 100 kHz (standard mode, the sensor's maximum).

Start Measurement is pointer 0x0021 (no data); poll 0x0202 for data ready, then write 0x03C4, wait 20 ms and read 24 bytes: eight big-endian 16-bit words, each followed by a CRC-8 (poly 0x31, init 0xFF). PM = uint16/10 µg/m³, RH = int16/100 %, T = int16/200 °C, VOC Index = int16/10.
The SEN54 has no NOx sensor: the 8th word is always unknown (0x7FFF; the datasheet says unknown values read 0xFFFF, the driver treats both as None).
PM readings settle after about 30 s and the VOC Index needs minutes to learn the baseline (it starts at 100).
Keep the metal shield floating: it is connected to GND inside the sensor.

driver.code:
# Sensirion SEN54 environmental sensor node (PM / RH / T / VOC Index), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the SEN5x datasheet (Version 2, March 2022), section 6: I2C address 0x69, max 100 kHz,
# no clock stretching. Commands are 16-bit pointers sent MSB first without CRC; every 2 data bytes
# are followed by a CRC-8 (poly 0x31, init 0xFF, CRC(0xBEEF) = 0x92).
# The SEN54 has no NOx sensor: the NOx word of "Read Measured Values" is always "unknown".
import time

FIELDS = ('pm1_0', 'pm2_5', 'pm4_0', 'pm10',   # mass concentration, ug/m3 (uint16, /10)
          'humidity',                          # compensated ambient RH, % (int16, /100)
          'temperature',                       # compensated ambient temperature, degC (int16, /200)
          'voc_index',                         # VOC Index, 1..500 (int16, /10)
          'nox_index')                         # NOx Index: always unknown (None) on the SEN54
_SCALE = (10, 10, 10, 10, 100, 200, 10, 10)
_SIGNED = (False, False, False, False, True, True, True, True)


def _crc8(data):
    crc = 0xFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = ((crc << 1) ^ 0x31) & 0xFF if crc & 0x80 else (crc << 1) & 0xFF
    return crc


class SEN54:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x69):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        time.sleep_ms(50)  # start-up time after power-on before I2C may be used (max 50 ms)

    def _cmd(self, ptr, data=b''):
        buf = bytearray([ptr >> 8, ptr & 0xFF])
        for i in range(0, len(data), 2):
            w = data[i:i + 2]
            buf += w + bytes([_crc8(w)])
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, buf)

    def _read(self, ptr, n_words, wait_ms=20):
        self._cmd(ptr)
        time.sleep_ms(wait_ms)  # datasheet: wait 20 ms before the read header
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n_words * 3)
        out = []
        for i in range(0, n_words * 3, 3):
            if _crc8(d[i:i + 2]) != d[i + 2]:
                raise OSError('SEN54 CRC mismatch: check wiring and 100 kHz bus speed')
            out.append((d[i] << 8) | d[i + 1])
        return out

    def start(self):
        """Enter Measurement-Mode (PM, RH/T and VOC; fan and laser on)."""
        self._cmd(0x0021)
        time.sleep_ms(50)

    def start_rht_gas_only(self):
        """Measure RH/T/VOC only (fan and laser off); PM values read as unknown."""
        self._cmd(0x0037)
        time.sleep_ms(50)

    def stop(self):
        self._cmd(0x0104)
        time.sleep_ms(200)

    def reset(self):
        self._cmd(0xD304)
        time.sleep_ms(100)

    def start_fan_cleaning(self):
        self._cmd(0x5607)
        time.sleep_ms(20)

    def device_status(self):
        w = self._read(0xD206, 2)
        return (w[0] << 16) | w[1]

    def data_ready(self):
        return (self._read(0x0202, 1)[0] & 0xFF) == 0x01

    def read(self, timeout_ms=3000):
        """Wait for a new measurement (one per second) and return a dict of the eight values.
        A value the sensor does not know (always NOx on the SEN54) is None."""
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not self.data_ready():
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('SEN54: no data (was start() called?)')
            time.sleep_ms(100)
        raw = self._read(0x03C4, 8)
        out = {}
        for name, r, scale, signed in zip(FIELDS, raw, _SCALE, _SIGNED):
            # Unknown: 0xFFFF (datasheet), 0x7FFF for int16 fields (Sensirion driver docs)
            if r == 0xFFFF or (signed and r == 0x7FFF):
                out[name] = None
                continue
            if signed and r & 0x8000:
                r -= 0x10000
            out[name] = r / scale
        return out

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sen54 import SEN54

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = SEN54(i2c)
sensor.start()

def f(v, fmt):
    return '--' if v is None else fmt % v

while True:
    m = sensor.read()
    print('PM1.0=%s PM2.5=%s PM4.0=%s PM10=%s ug/m3' % (f(m['pm1_0'], '%.1f'), f(m['pm2_5'], '%.1f'), f(m['pm4_0'], '%.1f'), f(m['pm10'], '%.1f')))
    print('RH=%s%% T=%sC VOC=%s NOx=%s' % (f(m['humidity'], '%.2f'), f(m['temperature'], '%.2f'), f(m['voc_index'], '%.0f'), f(m['nox_index'], '%.0f')))
    time.sleep(1)
